application_guidance.input_pattern: A gradient-tracking task allowing arbitrary line-interior fresh HVP queries.
read_original_when: Changing derivative-expectation interchange, oracle coupling or endpoint predictability.
sensitive_conditions: Endpoints must precede the fresh randomness.
The uniform line point is independent of the new oracle sample.
A robust output need not be unbiased; do not use it as a martingale difference without further argument.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Conditional unbiasedness/variance for Y; conditional probability at least 1-delta for the robust output.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Numerical constants; log(2/delta) explicitly avoids a degenerating logarithmic cost as delta approaches one.
complexity_scope.oracle: One new-sample HVP at x+Uh in direction h; new U and Z for every repetition.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: A vector approximating grad F(y)-grad F(x) in Euclidean norm.
complexity_scope.regime: All finite dimensions and predictable finite endpoints; arbitrary rho>0, delta in (0,1).
complexity_scope.resource: One fresh HVP per Y; a pathwise batch count determined by the already fixed endpoints, rho,delta and public scale bounds. Arithmetic is separate.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Random-line increment estimator only; no optimization stopping rule or minimax lower bound.

content.intended_use: Supply a fresh one-point HVP increment estimator and its conditional accuracy/cost interface.

proofs.full_local_argument: Condition on H and treat x,y,h as fixed. Put B(u)=Hess F(x+uh)h and N=(Hess f(x+Uh;Z)-Hess F(x+Uh))h. Independence and the stipulated Hessian unbiasedness give E[N|H,U]=0; the directional second-moment bound gives E[||N||^2|H,U]<=sigma2^2||h||^2. Since F is C^2 with L1-Lipschitz gradient, ||Hess F(z)||op<=L1, so ||B(u)||<=L1||h||. These bounds ensure integrability over U,Z and justify the conditional integrations. Differentiation-expectation interchange is a model assumption, not derived from sample smoothness. The fundamental theorem of calculus gives integral_0^1 B(u)du=grad F(y)-grad F(x)=mu, hence E[Y|H]=mu. Write Y-mu=N+B(U)-mu. Conditional centering of N makes its cross term with B(U)-mu zero. Therefore E[||Y-mu||^2|H]=E[||N||^2|H]+E[||B(U)-mu||^2|H]<=sigma2^2||h||^2+E[||B(U)||^2|H]<=V0||h||^2. Let K=max{1,ceil(36 V0||h||^2/rho^2)}. Conditional independence makes the average of K copies have variance at most V0||h||^2/K, so Chebyshev gives probability at least 3/4 of lying within rho/3 of mu. Generate R independent such averages, where R>=max{1,ceil(8 log(1/delta))}. Declare an average admissible when more than half of all averages lie within distance 2rho/3 of it; return the first admissible average, or the first average if none exists. This finite comparison selector is Borel. Hoeffding bounds the probability that at most half the averages are within rho/3 of mu by exp(-R/8)<=delta. On the complement a good average is admissible, and the strict-majority neighbor set of any admissible average intersects the good strict majority. Triangle inequality then places every admissible average within 2rho/3+rho/3=rho of mu. Thus the returned vector has the claimed confidence and uses exactly KR HVPs, bounded by the displayed O((1+V0||h||^2/rho^2)log(2/delta)). If h=0 then Y=0=mu and the same reasoning applies, or the component may return zero without calls. All assertions hold conditional on each realized admissible endpoint pair; unconditional probability follows by averaging. No unbiasedness is claimed for the selected robust average.
proofs.locator: p.6 equation (4.1); pp.11–12 Lemmas A.1 and A.3; explicit local constants supplied here
map: Condition on endpoints and then U; use derivative-expectation interchange and the fundamental theorem of calculus.
Split centered sample noise from the population line-point fluctuation; the cross term vanishes.
Average independent copies, then use an explicit robust-center selector.
proofs.omitted_details: None for the stated conditional local result. This does not prove an end-to-end SOSP algorithm.
proofs.reading_coverage: Initial image of p.11 and p.6 inspected; original-PDF p.12 proof read; Lemma A.1 selector is reproduced and checked locally.

assumptions: F=E f is C^2 and grad F is globally L1-Lipschitz; differentiation commutes with expectation through order two as required by Definition 3.1.
The jointly measurable sample loss has the regularity in Definition 3.1. For all deterministic z,v, E[(Hess f(z;Z)-Hess F(z))v]=0 and E||(Hess f(z;Z)-Hess F(z))v||^2<=sigma2^2||v||^2.

Endpoints and displacement are chosen before the current U and oracle sample. Each repeated draw uses a new independent U and sample after fixing its query point and direction. No persistent sample handle or paired endpoint query is used.
statement.conclusion: E[Y|H]=mu and E[||Y-mu||^2|H]<=V0||h||^2. Each Y costs one fresh HVP. A robust estimator Chord_rho(y,x) satisfies P(||Chord_rho-mu||<=rho|H)>=1-delta using O((1+V0||h||^2/rho^2) log(2/delta)) fresh HVPs. For delta<=1/2 this is the paper's O((1+V0||h||^2/rho^2) log(1/delta)) expression. The single-sample estimator is unbiased; unbiasedness of the robust selector is not asserted.
statement.objects_and_definitions: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space let h=y-x, V0=sigma2^2+L1^2, and mu=grad F(y)-grad F(x). Relative to a pre-estimator history H, x,y are finite H-measurable vectors. Draw U uniform on [0,1] independently of a fresh sample Z and H. Set Y=Hess f(x+Uh;Z)h.
statement.parameter_domains: Any finite d>=1; L1,sigma2 finite and nonnegative; rho>0; delta in (0,1). No tolerance relation, population gap, Hessian continuity modulus or almost-sure Hessian-noise bound is used in this local argument beyond the standing regularity needed for the line identity.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible F and oracle, every finite dimension and every such history-measurable pair of endpoints, the mean and variance claims hold conditional on H. For every rho>0 and 0<delta<1, independent repetitions give conditional error probability at most delta. Random endpoints need no unconditional second-moment bound for these conditional statements.

checked_locators: Definition 3.1; equation (4.1); Lemmas A.1/A.3 and complete local reconstruction
use_restrictions: Independent Reviewer must separately check the full local argument; no complete_local_argument_checked result is claimed here.
The log(2/delta) convention and explicit batching constants are a disclosed local completion of the paper's asymptotic presentation.
This result is an increment estimate, not a 2/3-success SOSP theorem.

facets.subject: New-sample HVP at an independently selected line point

research_use.reason: Replace biased deterministic quadrature by an unbiased one-point HVP sample.

source_refs.locator: p.5 Definition 3.1; p.6 equation (4.1); pp.11–12 Lemmas A.1 and A.3 and proof

summary: Predictable endpoints and an independent uniform line point yield an unbiased one-HVP gradient increment with conditional variance proportional to squared displacement and a robust high-probability estimator.
title: Fresh random-line HVP gradient increment
use_when: Estimate a population gradient difference without evaluating the same sample at two points.
